rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause. The handbook is scanned cold (self-study, no trainer voice to fill a clever header). Two clauses, both required. Squint — names the concept: cover the bullets; the header still names the ONE thing the student walks away holding. A claim when the slide argues ("Passing is not proof", "Find is easier than judge", "Gates decay"); a named thing when it names one ("The lethal trifecta"). Failure modes: empty containers ("The move", "The names", "The spirit", "The question", "The territory") head anything and name nothing; orphan mood/mystery ("Trained twice", "A different country", "The ghost, drawn solid") pays off only after the body; orientation ("You are here", "Back to the map") carries position not concept, rationed to ONE beat per arc lecture; no two slides share a header (one-page render). Truth — asserts what the body supports: the squint pass is orthogonal to correctness, and sharpening is where a header slips into a lie (a crisp header is easier to believe). No category errors (whole named for a part — "the loop is an eval" when the eval is the *check* the loop runs), no dropped qualifiers ("unchecked", "reliably"), no unsupported universals ("every", "always", "unchanged", "breaks"); named at the strength the body licenses. Inherit: no pedagogy/contemplative headers (§ check_student_facing #23), no em-dashes (#14), declarative noun-phrases or claims not command verbs (#17 lecture carve-out) except where the slide's payload is a live do-move ("See the loop in your live session"). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A prompt inside a lecture is a trainer show-and-tell, never a room follow-along. (Antti 2026-08-20, stated as general.) Lectures are projected; the trainer runs the prompt on the demo repo and reads the return out loud. The room watches. This holds for every `{{prompt:<key>}}` / inline `Prompt` block in `curriculum/lectures/` — 20 blocks across 9 files as of 2026-08-20 — and it is the DEFAULT, so a lecture prompt needs no per-file permission. The failure it prevents: an imperative aimed at the room (*"Ask Claude to propose five hooks"*) reads as a task, and a task inside a closer converts a recognition beat into work — a 2026-08-20 persona run scored exactly that slide 5/10, the lowest beat in the AE101 corpus, on a lecture whose job is to name what the student already felt. Exercises are where a student's own hands go; a lecture that wants one is asking for the wrong surface. Author's move: keep the prompt, cut any second-person imperative to run it, and give the room its stance in the body (*"This one runs on the screen — watch the list come back rather than typing along"*), with the trainer's instruction in the maintainer block. `check_slides.md` §4 is the same remedy generalised: setup on the slide, doing in trainer delivery. Not covered: exercise prompts, prework prompts, and prompts on reference/supplementary pages, all of which the student runs themselves. Carve-out, the answer must be theirs (Antti 2026-08-20): where the prompt's value is that the STUDENT's own session answers it, a trainer demo returns the wrong machine's answer and destroys the beat. `the-agent-loop.md`'s `## See the loop in your live session` runs three prompts against the session that will carry the student's send-off, so the tool list that comes back has to be theirs; `when-a-plan-is-good.md` sits beside *"Enter plan mode in your own session right now."* Those stay student-run and say so in the body.
